page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d3c.7xlarge is a big data-focused virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.9 GHz, providing 28 dedicated vCPUs alongside 112.0 GB of system memory. This establishes a balanced allocation ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per core, intended to handle concurrent execution pipelines without memory starvation.

The defining feature of this instance configuration is its integrated high-capacity storage, bundling 27,487 GB of local HDD storage directly onto the host. Unlike NVMe-based systems that prioritize high random IOPS, this architecture delivers massive storage capacity suited for sequential data processing. Network operations are supported by a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, accommodating large data ingests and inter-node cluster synchronizations. There are no accelerated graphics processing units included.

From an infrastructure and cost efficiency perspective, bundling massive local hard disk storage provides economical data density per compute node compared to attaching elastic network block storage volumes. However, reliance on rotating magnetic media represents a performance tradeoff, favoring high sequential throughput over low-latency transactional access. As a result, the instance is well suited for big data architectures, distributed file systems, Hadoop or MapReduce clusters, log aggregation pipelines, and large-scale data lake indexing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d3c.7xlarge is a big data instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.9 GHz, it features 28 dedicated vCPUs and 112.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance stands out with its substantial 27,487 GB of local HDD storage, offering high storage density directly attached to the host, alongside a 16 Gbps baseline network throughput. It does not include GPU acceleration. The dense mechanical storage architecture provides a cost-effective design for storing and streaming vast datasets, though it trades off random I/O latency compared to solid-state drives. This hardware profile matches the requirements of large-scale distributed analytics, Hadoop data nodes, batch processing, and log archiving frameworks.
